claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's good to know you're inquiring about your son Alex.

To help me assess his eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand more about your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex was born in March 2006, so he's 19 now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I need to check the eligibility rules to ensure I'm giving you accurate guidance about Alex's age and Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the eligibility rules that Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16, but can continue if a child is 16 or over and stays in approved education or training (up to age 20).

Since Alex is 19 years old, he would need to be in approved education or training to qualify.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know Alex is in approved education.

Before I can make my final assessment, I need to clarify one more important detail:

**Are you living with Alex, or are you paying towards his care (such as food, clothes, or other living expenses)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on the eligibility rules:

- Alex is 19 years old
- He is currently in approved education (studying for A-levels at sixth form college)
- He lives with you

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16. However, you'll normally still qualify if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. Since Alex is 19 and in approved education, he meets the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. 

Since he is 19 years old, in approved education (A-levels), and living with you, all the conditions for eligibility are met. You can continue to receive Child Benefit for him, as long as he remains in approved education. This eligibility will continue until he reaches age 20 or leaves approved education, whichever comes first.

If you'd like to apply or have any other questions about Child Benefit, you can contact HMRC or visit the official government website for more information on how to make a claim.
